html:
Buddhism began in India, but between about 600 and 1200 CE it faded there almost completely, even as it grew across the rest of Asia.

There was no single cause. Historians point to several:

  • Buddhism lived in large monasteries that depended on kings and rich merchants. After the Guptas, long-distance trade shrank and most kings gave their land grants to Brahmins and temples.
  • Hindu worship changed and competed well. The bhakti saints offered a warm personal faith in local languages. Shankara took over much Buddhist method. The Buddha himself came to be counted as a form of Vishnu.
  • The Huna invasions ruined the monasteries of the northwest. The pilgrim Xuanzang, about 640, already found many empty.

The last stronghold was the east, under the Pala kings, with the great monastery-universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila. Around 1200 the armies of Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed them (see the conquest of Bengal), and the monks fled to Nepal and Tibet.

Buddhism lived on in Sri Lanka, the Himalayas and Chittagong. It returned to India in the 20th century, above all with Ambedkar's mass conversion of 1956.
sum: Buddhism began in India, but between about 600 and 1200 CE it faded there almost completely, even as it grew across the rest of Asia.
